summary.text: 哪 is used to ask “which?” or “where?” It is written with 口 on the left and 那 on the right; the usual analysis assigns 口 a meaning role and 那 a sound role, though the historical basis of that sound role is not settled.

formation.text: The usual analysis treats 哪 as a phonosemantic compound: 口 contributes a meaning cue, while 那 is assigned a phonetic role. Later lexicographic testimony says the graph was originally 那, but does not date the addition of 口 or establish a sequence of forms.

components.text: The left-hand 口 contributes a meaning cue in the usual analysis, though its precise contribution to 哪 is not specified.
The right-hand 那 is assigned a sound role. Later lexicographic testimony also says 哪 was originally written 那, without dating that spelling.

sound_limitation.text: Available Baxter–Sagart data gives 那 as Middle Chinese na and Old Chinese *nˤar, but supplies no corresponding reconstruction for 哪. The modern reading pair does not establish their historical sound relation.

sound.text: In current principal Mandarin readings, 哪 is nǎ and 那 is nà. This present-day comparison does not demonstrate the historical basis of 那’s proposed sound role in 哪.

history.text: 哪 is not recorded in 說文. Later lexicographic testimony describes it as a particle spelling and says it was originally written 那; this does not establish a dated sequence of forms. The selected image is a modern rendering of the graph.

哪 is also recorded in 哪哪 for a sound made by performers in nuo exorcism rites and in 咄哪 as a personal name. A variant with 舟 is attributed to graphic similarity and does not explain the standard graph’s origin.

uncertainties.text: The beginning of 哪’s written use for “which” or “where” is undated. Proposals deriving spoken forms from 奈何 or 若何 differ and concern the words’ origins; they do not establish the graph’s ancestry. No matched reconstructed readings for 哪 and 那 are provided.

senses.text: Later lexicographic testimony describes 哪 as a spelling for a particle, originally written 那. The first use of 哪 for this word is not dated.

senses.gloss: sound made by performers in nuo exorcism rites
senses.text: 哪哪 is recorded as the sound made by performers in nuo exorcism rites; the cited record does not date this use.

senses.gloss: personal name element in 咄哪
senses.text: 哪 is recorded in the personal name 咄哪. This compound citation does not establish an independent single-character meaning.
哪 is used for “which” and “where”; the beginning of this written usage is not dated.

senses.period: Qing citation; exact first use unresolved
senses.text: A Qing play citation records 哪 used rhetorically to mean “how”; it does not establish the first occurrence.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a chronology connecting the particle, ritual cry, personal name, “which/where,” and rhetorical “how.” Competing proposals about the spoken words do not demonstrate semantic development or graphic ancestry.

overview.text: 哪 asks “which?” or “where?” It is written with 口 on the left and 那 on the right; the usual analysis assigns them meaning and sound roles, respectively.

components.text: 口 contributes a meaning cue, though its precise contribution here is not specified.

The current principal Mandarin readings are 哪 nǎ and 那 nà. This is a present-day comparison; their different tones do not explain the proposed sound role, and the pair alone does not establish the historical relation.
